James Corvin, first entry. Today we began the assembly of my tank, Black Rock. Installed the turret. Composite construction of cast elements welded together. I approve of this design. It’s practical.

Regarding our investigation—thorough examination of the island has disproven our theory. There is no top-secret Moretti bunker beneath us.

This Moretti operated methodically, creating an entire network of false facilities and fabricated documents to confuse us.

We've wasted too much time following a false lead. We need to reconsider our approach and act more thoughtfully—and base our every step on solid, proven facts.

Side plates installed today. A little extra protection is never a bad idea.

Moretti's records shed light on the events at Morgenlicht. It was there that scientists accidentally discovered the KRONOS prototype's tendency to generate unexpected results by making probabilistic errors. This capacity for controlled error could be fine-tuned and honed—to generate unconventional solutions on demand.

All they needed to unlock truly groundbreaking inventions was to increase computational power. Literally, by scaling up the machine's size. Exponentially.

Today we painted the tank black. The dark camouflage will give an additional psychological advantage over the enemy and enhance effectiveness during night operations.

In our investigation, everything has fallen into place: KRONOS is a colossal computing system capable of "creative mutations." And it is indeed the source of all these impossible technologies we've found in secret bunkers and that the Architect is distributing via satellite. Incredible.

Moretti’s notes show that initially he admired his creation and believed he had built a tool capable of "designing humanity's future." But after that it gets more interesting.

Installed the smoke mortars today. Seemingly unassuming components. But smoke screens have saved my previous tanks from destruction more than once.

The tone of Moretti's notes changes dramatically. He was always cautious and never trusted anyone too much. But at some point, he becomes completely paranoid. He suspects not only the scientists, engineers, and staff, but KRONOS itself. He literally writes that he's convinced the machine has gained "self-awareness" and is manipulating people.

The further we go, the more paranoid Moretti's entries become. Now we face a new mystery: was Moretti himself gradually descending into madness, or had he truly created something that transcended its programmed capabilities?

We've installed a muzzle break, which will significantly reduce recoil. With that, the gun is finished.

In Moretti's final entry, it appears he completely lost control of himself. He writes that the machine is pretending, that it "knows everything." He explicitly calls for its destruction before it's too late.

But there's nothing after that entry. We haven't found a single piece of evidence about KRONOS's subsequent fate. Was the machine really destroyed, or is it still operating somewhere in the snows of Antarctica? That would be frightening, especially considering the Architect's actions.

What if he possesses even more recent KRONOS developments that are once again a decade ahead of our capabilities?

The tank is now outfitted with all essentials. It'll be ready very soon.

And just in time, too. Now we know what Moretti was hiding from us and where the Architect got all these technologies, we're left with our main mission—to find KRONOS.

We're already preparing a military search operation in Antarctica. But why do I feel like this is all another one of Moretti's deceptions? Did Moretti even exist at all? After all his hoaxes, you start questioning everything and considering even the most out-there theories. Leni proposed that the Architect and Moretti might be the same person. And Teddy is absolutely convinced that the Architect is actually KRONOS itself.

Whoever the Architect may be, he's several steps ahead of us. We need to find KRONOS to stop the Architect.

The tracks are installed. Black Rock is finally complete. Each component calibrated, every system tested. An engineering marvel ready to rise to any challenge.

Throughout my career, I've commanded many tanks, but this one is something special. It represents the culmination of our efforts, recovered technologies, and our determination to counter the threat posed by the Architect.

Whatever he has planned, whatever secrets await us in Antarctica or elsewhere, this machine improves our probability of success.

History teaches us that preparation is the decisive factor between victory and defeat. I'm confident this will hold true in the battle that lies ahead.

Today we installed the suspension components. Nothing out of the ordinary. But the design is reliable, field-tested.

We're still examining shipping manifests where Moretti's pseudonyms appear. Thanks to transport vessel routes and data from the Architect's satellite, we've located several dozen secret facilities.

In these, we've found new blueprints and records created as part of Project KRONOS. But this doesn’t bring us any closer to understanding how German scientists managed to develop all these designs, nor to finding the main KRONOS bunker where something truly grand and dangerous was being built.

We installed road wheels today. The suspension system is nearly complete. This part is simple.

Our investigation, however, remains challenging. What are we missing? Where in Europe could a secret bunker of such magnitude be concealed that we've failed to locate it thus far?

Teddy suggests the facility might be underwater. He noted that submarine departure dates frequently aligned with transport vessel schedules. An intriguing observation, but constructing an underwater base in the 1940s would have been beyond even Moretti's capabilities.

Teddy proposed another theory—that the secret base might be on the moon. We dismissed this immediately. The Architect only managed to launch a satellite recently. In the 1940s, space travel was the stuff of fantasy.

Commander's observation equipment installed. The rotating periscope provides complete 360-degree visibility. I can monitor the battlefield without being in the turret itself—sounds promising.

We've identified unusual activity patterns from a fleet of small cargo vessels. They would leave port and return empty several hours later. According to ship logs, they always headed to the same coordinates in open water.

Could it really be an underwater base?

Leni shares my skepticism about this theory. However, she finds the transfer of containers to submarines more plausible. We need to determine where the submarines from this sector were headed.

Crew observation equipment installed today. At its core is a television-based observation system—another piece of KRONOS technology that's decades ahead of its time.

Intelligence archives indicate increased submarine activity in the South Atlantic near the Argentine coast, with suspected movement patterns toward Antarctica. Recently deciphered documents confirm this theory.

Antarctica appears to be the final destination for these shipments. The most remote location on Earth would indeed be the ideal place to hide something of this magnitude. Now we just need to determine what exactly Moretti wanted to conceal in the ice.

Installed a pair of Browning M2HB heavy machine guns. The remote control system allows us to engage targets without exposing the crew to return fire—a tactical advantage I value highly.

We thought we were closing in on the truth about what Moretti was building, only to discover inconsistencies in the schematics of this gigantic Wunderwaffe from recently decrypted KRONOS archives. The blueprints contain deliberate errors that would render any assembled device inoperable.

Damn! Another of Moretti's falsifications.

What exactly was he hiding behind such elaborate disinformation? What could possibly be more classified than a Wunderwaffe?

Main gun finally installed. A very unusual specimen of special caliber with an ejector that will ensure high accuracy and rate of fire. Exactly what I need.

After analyzing and separating authentic blueprints from forgeries, we've made a breakthrough discovery: the "wonder weapon" we've been searching for isn't a weapon at all, but a computing center of incredible scale.

I must acknowledge Moretti's genius in creating such an elaborate smokescreen of false projects and secret bases. Without the data from the Architect's satellite, we'd still be a long way away from this revelation.

Fenders and mudguards installed today. Nothing special, but they're another step toward completing the tank.

Our investigation, however, has yielded something special. We've uncovered Moretti's personal records. He writes about creating a mechanical-electronic system capable of not just computing, but "predicting" new ideas.

This appears to be the true KRONOS—the genuine source of all these incredible technologies. A machine that could design other machines.

But how is it possible? Or is this just another of Moretti's elaborate deceptions—perhaps meant to distract intelligence agencies from an actual working "wonder weapon"?

Infrared spotlights connected. These devices allow for combat operations in night conditions. A necessary minimum by today's standards.

We're still deciphering Moretti's records. He writes that his machine was initially conceived as a giant engineering tool, but due to numerous design flaws, it began to "hallucinate," generating answers, theories, and concepts that hadn't existed before. Most of this output was nonsensical, but among the chaos were genuine innovations.

"Mistakes lead to new discoveries. The perfect lacks creative spark. Everything obeys the laws of nature. Even machines." Hmm...

Nebel speaking, log entry one. Today, construction of my Windhund vehicle has begun.

Installed additional spaced armor. Valuable component. Such armor is effective against shaped charge shells.

Our investigation also started today. Documents marked "KRONOS" contain technologies decades ahead of our current capabilities. Designs from the 1940s that simply shouldn't exist. Some match the data being transmitted by the Architect's satellite.

So far, we've found only one lead: references to "Schloss Morgenlicht." Morning Light Castle. We must locate this place and discover what activities were conducted there.

Mobile tactical ground-based pulse-Doppler radar. Impressive technology. Can identify target size and range. A skilled operator, like me, obviously, can distinguish between personnel, animals and vehicles from significant distances. Much more compact than anything we have available today.

And all this thanks to a radar schematic from 1944 we found in the KRONOS archives. This technology isn't just ahead of its time—it's ahead of ours, too.

If only I'd had this in my hands back then, I would have changed the course of history...

Standard tank lighting system, rearview mirrors, and communications antennas. Nothing remarkable—just basic equipment for any modern combat vehicle.

What is remarkable, though, is what we've learned about mid-1944. Something changed dramatically at Morgenlicht then: trucks began arriving during daylight hours, and one more wing of the clinic was completely handed over to Moranti.

The timing coincides precisely with when the Reich was desperately trying to develop its "Wunderwaffe". Hmm...

Smoke grenade launchers installed today. Effective for quick deployment of concealing smoke screens at close range.

Our Moranti created his own concealing screen, which we're still trying to disperse.

In documents from that period, we found mentions that his "Geistesfessel" experiment—"Mind Shackles"—was successful and ready for expansion.

Sends chills down my spine when I start imagining what he must have done to those scientists to obtain all these technologies.

Outfitted the tank with the necessary entrenching tools. You can have the most advanced radar system, but sometimes you need to get your hands dirty to get out of trouble.

In one of the secret bunkers we discovered, we found fragments of Morgenlicht's medical documentation. It contained a list of disturbing procedure names: "Thought Collection," "Mist Chamber," "Dream Catcher," "Mind Bridge," "Mechanical Memory," "Shadow Archive."

The jigsaw is slowly coming together. I can feel we're getting closer to the truth—and soon we'll find the missing pieces.

Vehicle is almost complete. Secured my favorite camouflage nets today. Concealment is my specialty—both hiding myself and finding those who try to disappear.

But tracking down Moranti has proven much more difficult. At some point, he suddenly vanishes from all documents, like he was eliminated as an unnecessary witness. But the experiments at Morgenlicht continued even without him.

What really happened? Another staged disappearance? Or did Moranti cross some line? What could he have done that was beyond acceptable limits even for the Reich?

Windhund is ready. Final systems check has been completed.

This isn't just another combat vehicle. It's a predator created for hunting—stealthy, lethal at long distances, and capable of dissolving into the night.

The hunt finally begins.

Now our investigation will accelerate significantly. Some secrets can only be uncovered through fieldwork.

Hatches installed today. Convenient placement for rapid entry and exit. Practical, efficient. Exactly what I need.

Found more information about Schloss Morgenlicht. It's a medical facility with a secret wing, located in a castle.

Records mention the facility's supervisor - a "Doctor Moranti."

A medical institution with a secret department? Something doesn't add up here. We need to determine how it's connected to Project KRONOS and the encrypted blueprints.

First part of suspension system installed. Another step closer to completing Windhund.

While studying the archives, we discovered a disturbing pattern. In 1943, prominent German scientists and engineers were systematically declared "insane" and disappeared at the Morgenlicht clinic.

Too organized to be coincidental. These weren't random outbreaks of mental illness. This was deliberate collection of intellectual resources.

Question is: what exactly were they doing with those resources?

Road wheels installed. Four on each side. The front pair has metal rims instead of rubber. Standard rubber would deteriorate too quickly under that weight distribution.

Found a former Morgenlicht orderly. His testimony is quite revealing. Military trucks under armed guard regularly arrived at the restricted wing. They brought people diagnosed with "manic depression."

So they were keeping scientists and engineers locked up. And under pressure, these captives were inventing new technologies? Is this what Project KRONOS was all about?

Dust screens mounted on sides today. They'll increase the vehicle's endurance on long missions. Definitely a welcome addition.

Found intriguing information in recovered Morgenlicht documents. An engineer officially declared "killed in action" in 1943 appears in the clinic's intake logs three weeks later.

But was this forced confinement? Some evidence suggests certain specialists went there voluntarily, accepting staged deaths to continue working under Moranti's protection. A clever trick to hide their research from Allied intelligence.

So who are you, Dr. Moranti? And how come I still don't know anything about you?

We’ve installed a muzzle brake on the main gun. It significantly reduces recoil. Just what I need.

Found a nurse's diary from Morgenlicht. She describes "Doctor Moranti" commanding both guards and patients with absolute authority. However, this doctor doesn't appear in any German medical registry or military archive. A true phantom.

This only confirms my suspicions—there was no Doctor Moranti, just an alias created specifically for Project KRONOS. Someone preferred to pull the strings from the shadows.

Applied base camouflage. Black. I must admit, the black is the reason I joined Sector 3. That and the chance to track down a few more war criminals. And to build my dream combat vehicle. Fine. There were multiple reasons.

The documents we've uncovered show patients at Morgenlicht were creating revolutionary designs while subjected to "special procedures."

No explanations about what these procedures entailed, but the reports track "productivity increases" after each session. Whatever they were doing to these scientists, it was systematic and delivered expected results. One more mystery for us to solve.

Low light level television camera mounted today. Remarkable technology. Can detect targets in near-total darkness. Resolution exceeds anything I've worked with before.

We were able to produce a prototype based on optical surveillance system schematics from Project KRONOS. The designs were likely created using patient ideas. I don't even want to think about what methods Moranti used to extract these concepts from them.

I hope he's still alive so we can find him. Justice never tires.

Infrared spotlight. Proven technology. I've used these before. Significantly improves target acquisition in darkness. And working in darkness is what I enjoy most.

We've discovered evidence of equipment being transported out of Morgenlicht in early 1944. Documents mention "special crates" moved under armed guard.

This means the clinic wasn't just a place for "extracting scientific concepts." They were also creating equipment prototypes there. Looks like Moranti was hiding an advanced design bureau in plain sight.

First recording, Miroslav Kotva here, but everyone just calls me Teddy. Finally starting the assembly of my tank—the Dravec! Today, we mounted the turret. Welded construction, rolled armor. It's a beauty!

The process is moving at full speed, and soon I'll have a new steel friend.

But our investigation seems to have hit a dead end.

We learned so much about this Morgenlicht clinic. Almost got to the bottom of it. And then suddenly we discovered that in mid-'44 there was a fire there. Everyone who knew the truth—patients, guards, staff—is officially listed as missing.

Smells as fishy as a whole fish market on fire. Hah! Not my best joke.

Today we finally started applying the camouflage to the tank. Pure black—sleek and intimidating, just how I like it. Some say black makes you a more visible target, but they don't understand the psychological effect. When an enemy sees a pitch-black tank emerging from the fog, they freeze.

Leni and our engineers are increasingly convinced that KRONOS is some kind of electromagnetic weapon. We've found blueprints for enormous radio tubes, powerful generators, and complex cooling systems.

There's just one thing I don't understand—if it's such a powerful electromagnetic cannon, why give it such a boring name? "KRONOS." Something doesn't add up.

Today the Dravec got its 902 Tucha system. The perfect addition to my black predator! Now I can disappear in a cloud of smoke in a matter of seconds. As my grandfather used to say: "A smart warrior knows when to be seen and when to vanish."

We've traced KRONOS equipment shipments to the North Sea coast, but then the trail goes cold.

Massive transport loads, specialized equipment, tons of materials—all delivered to coastal facilities, and then...nothing. No records whatsoever of where everything went next.

This Moretti really didn't want anyone following his tracks.

We installed the laser rangefinder today. It's amazing technology— determines distance to target with incredible precision. My Dravec is getting more new toys every day!

Speaking of lasers—we're using KRONOS technology for this rangefinder. But our technicians had to rework everything. The original blueprints were drawn to a strange scale. Almost as if it was supposed to be a massive combat laser.

The deeper we dig, the more questions we have. Was Moretti trying to build some kind of death ray? Sounds like something from those science fiction novels I read as a boy...but looking at these KRONOS schematics, I'm ready to believe anything.

Today we installed a new muzzle brake on the gun. It's a masterpiece! It significantly reduces recoil, which makes firing much more comfortable.

But that's nothing. What we recently discovered...in one of the KRONOS documents, there's a description of a massive bunker built into coastal cliffs. Exact location not specified, of course—Moretti wouldn't give us a gift like that—but the scale itself is staggering.

If the dimensions are accurate, there's enough space to hide something truly gigantic...

I'm willing to bet that's where Moretti was assembling his Wunderwaffe.

Today we secured everything we might need to the tank: towing cables, smoke canisters, underwater driving equipment—the works. A good tank, like a good soldier, must be ready for anything.

And we have plenty to be ready for. We've been studying maps of the North Sea...

That bunker Moretti built is located on Norwegian islands. And we strongly suspect it's right on the same island where that American missile base was—the one those mercenaries captured and launched the satellite from.

So it's right under our noses? Somewhere directly beneath us? All this time we've been sitting on top of the main KRONOS bunker?!

The Dravec is ready! My new steel friend is armed and dangerous. Fast, armored, and with enough firepower to make enemies see their life flash before their eyes when my gun barrel points their way.

Just look at those elegant lines and that menacing silhouette! It'll haunt our enemies' nightmares.

What adventures await us—and what stories I'll be able to tell later!

Let the hunt begin!

Installed the running gear. The suspension is a masterpiece! It'll make the thing so smooth to ride, I'll be able to enjoy my coffee without spilling a drop. Well...not literally, of course. There'll still be some vibration. It is a tank, after all.

Our investigation is moving forward again, too. We thought the case with the Morgenlicht fire was closed, but then Leni discovered something strange—the KRONOS blueprints we're using to build our tanks were created AFTER the fire.

As they say in those detective novels—the plot thickens!

Finally got my commander's cupola! It's absolutely brilliant—comes with a full set of observation devices that are a tanker's dream. I like the TKN-1 night vision system the most—lets me see in the dark, like a cat.

We've developed a new theory about this whole KRONOS business. Either the patients' work was removed before the fire and processed somewhere else, or...and here's where it gets interesting...what if these "mad scientists" were just a cover story? What if the real source of these technologies isn't them at all?

We added extra armor plating around the turret today—five powerful blocks filled with polyurethane and steel plates. Excellent protection against shaped charges. Can't wait to see how it holds up in combat!

Meanwhile, it turns out Leni was right all along. There never was any "Doctor Moranti!" It was just one of dozens of pseudonyms used by the real mastermind—someone named Alessandro Moretti.

Why would one man need so many names? Couldn't he decide which one he liked best?

We installed the main gun today, and I can't wait to fire it! When you pull the trigger and feel the whole machine shudder...nothing quite compares to that feeling.

Turns out this Moretti is a very interesting character. He wasn't just an engineer—he was a master at building secret facilities. And then, in '43, he completely disappears from all official records.

And guess what? That's exactly when our "Doctor Moranti" suddenly appears! Then, after the Morgenlicht fire, the pseudonyms from our list suddenly start showing up in shipping manifests and other documents.

Today we installed the active protection system. It's an absolute revolution—it can detect incoming shells in a split second. Mind-blowing!

By the way, we discovered something unexpected about Morgenlicht. Turns out it wasn't a prison or torture laboratory like we thought. It was just one link in a network of carefully disguised research centers.

Seems our friend Moretti dreamed of becoming a horror writer. So much effort put into creating this cover, so many details in fake reports. Such talent gone to waste!

Today we installed a thermal sleeve on the gun barrel. It's a good piece of kit—stops weather conditions affecting barrel accuracy.

And Moretti keeps throwing us new puzzles. We've traced the supply chains connected to all those pseudonyms. Dozens of factories were involved in this Project KRONOS—electronics manufacturers, chemical plants, textile mills...and strangely enough, huge amber shipments.

What the hell do they need amber for? And where did he get so much? Did Moretti steal the Amber Room or something?

Today we installed the Oplot-MO active protection system, and it's really something! The radar detects anti-tank missiles flying at 600-800 m/s and automatically activates a six-barrel anti-aircraft gun that shoots them down right in mid-air. KRONOS has competition, because we've got some pretty impressive technology of our own!

This Moretti...he's completely thrown me off. I was just starting to believe his story about mad scientists who drew him crazy blueprints, and now we're discovering he was building something big.

But where did he get all these blueprints and technologies from?

My Dravec is getting closer to completion. Buddy, soon we'll be heading into adventures worthy of a Hollywood movie!

I'd make a film about KRONOS too. But tickets would only be sold to people with level five security clearance—an exclusive audience.

Shame, because it would be quite a spectacle. Among the KRONOS blueprints, we've found something suspicious—component schemes pointing to some kind of Wunderwaffe. Nobody can figure out what, exactly.

But whatever it was, it needed enough power to run an entire city.

󠀰Today we begin building my new weapon for future assignments.󠀲󠀠󠀳 Right from the design stage, I chose a wheeled platform over a tracked one: wheels are quiet, fast on the road, and capable enough off it.󠀲󠀡󠀳 󠀰Just what I need for my work.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀰We've fitted the suspension parts and a drive for each wheel—a sensible choice for a vehicle of this class.󠀲󠀣󠀳

󠀰I've received an assignment: five targets, top priority.󠀲󠀤󠀳 󠀰Each of them has access to data from the Architect's satellite.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀥󠀳The first is an arms dealer from Marseille.󠀲󠀦󠀳 󠀰He's got ties to three groups in the region, and he'll sell to anyone.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀧󠀳󠀲󠀨󠀳The second and third are ex-military.󠀲󠀩󠀳 󠀰They intercepted blueprints for gunfire sound suppression systems.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀳 󠀰One of them has access to a production facility, which makes him even more dangerous: not only can he store the tech, he can also make weapons with it.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀳󠀰The fourth and fifth are intermediaries.󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀳 󠀰Lower priority, but their channels need to be shut down.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀳󠀰The technologies they possess could enhance my vehicle.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀳 󠀰Time to get started.

Using the KRONOS blueprints obtained in Tangier, we made a suppressor for the 105-mm gun based on a chambered system for diverting powder gases.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀨󠀳 󠀰󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀨󠀳It significantly reduces sound on firing.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀩󠀳 󠀰Not complete silence, but an advantage.

󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀠󠀳󠀰I checked Erich's other targets.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀡󠀳 󠀰One's already been taken out.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀢󠀳 󠀰An arms dealer in Lisbon with ties to mercenaries in North Africa.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀣󠀳 󠀰󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀤Dangerous, but not connected to the satellite.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀥󠀳 󠀰He didn't have access to KRONOS technology, and󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀦󠀳 󠀰I couldn't find him in any Sector 3 reports.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀧󠀳 󠀰Erich eliminated him on his own initiative.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀨󠀳 󠀰The man deserved an investigation, maybe a trial.󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀩󠀳 󠀰But not a bullet without proof.

󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀡󠀳󠀰Erich is right nine times out of ten.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀢󠀳 󠀰The problem is the tenth.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀣󠀳 󠀰Without supervision, even the best make mistakes.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀤󠀳 󠀰One man can't be intelligence, judge, and executioner all at once.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀥󠀳 󠀰It's too much. Mistakes are inevitable.

We've connected the headlights.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀧󠀳 󠀰Standard work.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀨󠀳 󠀰The assembly continues, and so does the investigation.

󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀩󠀳Erich's notebook lists the next target.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀡󠀳 󠀰A man with ties to dangerous circles.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀢󠀳 󠀰There's no direct proof of his guilt, but there is circumstantial evidence. Enough to place him under surveillance, but not to take him out.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀥󠀳 󠀰Erich, though, decided otherwise.

󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀦󠀳I know how this ends.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀧󠀳 󠀰I saw it back in '45.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀨󠀳 󠀰He was certain back then, too. And he was right.󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀩󠀳 󠀰But he crossed a line, and then the classified details came to light.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀡󠀳

󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀢󠀳󠀰I won't be able to change his mind.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀣󠀳 󠀰I couldn't back then.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀤󠀳 󠀰Now, when he's worked alone for so many years with no supervision, there's even less chance.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀥󠀳 󠀰We're not in a movie.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀦󠀳 󠀰I can't risk it.

󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀧󠀳I need to act.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀨󠀳 󠀰There's no time to wait for a reply from Sector 3.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀩󠀳 󠀰It's damned ironic.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀠󠀳 󠀰I'm doing exactly what Erich is: acting alone, with no system.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀡󠀳 󠀰But there's a difference.

The vehicle is being assembled without me for now.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀣󠀳 󠀰It's being fitted out with everything it needs.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀤󠀳 󠀰Meanwhile, I'm needed elsewhere.

󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀥󠀳󠀰I'm calculating Erich's firing position.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀦󠀳 󠀰It's not hard.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀧󠀳 󠀰I know how he thinks, because I think the same way.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀨󠀳 󠀰He'll choose an elevated spot around three to four hundred meters away, a firing area with an escape route across a rooftop or through an alley.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀩󠀳 󠀰East of the target, so that the sun's behind him in the morning.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀠󠀳󠀰I found the only suitable spot.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀡󠀳 󠀰If he's as good as I remember, this is where he'll come.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀢󠀳I've taken up a position opposite, two hundred meters away.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀣󠀳 󠀰Two hundred meters.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀤󠀳 󠀰I'm ready.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀥󠀳 󠀰I checked the wind, the light, the escape routes.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀦󠀳 󠀰I thought back to how we used to work together.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀧󠀳 󠀰Back then, everything was flawless: two shooters, one mission.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰Now there are still two shooters.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀩󠀳 󠀰But they're on opposite sides of the sight.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀠󠀳

The mechanics have fitted an infrared spotlight on the vehicle. An indispensable tool for working with targets in low-visibility conditions at long range.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀢󠀳 󠀰But that's for later.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀣󠀳 󠀰For now, I'm working in the morning sun.

󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀤Erich appeared at dawn.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀥󠀳 󠀰Quietly, professionally, he took up his position.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀦󠀳 󠀰The one I predicted he would.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀩󠀳 󠀰He set up his rifle, checked the wind, then settled behind the scope.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀠󠀳󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀢󠀳󠀰I'm watching him through the optics.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀣󠀳 󠀰Two hundred meters.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀤󠀳 󠀰Wind at one and a half knots, steady.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀥󠀳 󠀰Minimal correction, everything calculated.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀦󠀳 Finger on the trigger.󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀩󠀳

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰At the last moment, he freezes.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀠󠀳 󠀰He's sensed something.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀡󠀳 󠀰It's his instinct.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀢󠀳 󠀰Seven years of solo work have sharpened his senses to the fullest.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀣󠀳 󠀰Slowly, he pulls away from the scope, turns his head, and looks in my direction.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀤󠀳 He's found me.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀧󠀳He recognizes me—I can tell by the way he's angled his head.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀨󠀳 It's the same gesture he always used to say: "Understood."

Today we fitted additional side protection: rubber screens.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀡󠀳 󠀰The vehicle is almost ready.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀢󠀳 󠀰There are dangerous operations ahead, and I'll need more than a rifle.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀣󠀳I passed the remaining names from Erich's notebook to the Sector 3 analysts.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀤󠀳 󠀰If they're connected to the Architect's satellite, they'll be added to my list.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀥󠀳 󠀰If not, others will deal with them.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀦󠀳Erich believed that a single person free of rules works faster and more precisely than a system.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀧󠀳 󠀰Nine times out of ten, he was right.󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀨󠀳 󠀰But with no supervision, nine times out of ten is a lottery, not accuracy.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀩󠀳Operating as a lone wolf means confusing justice with revenge, sooner or later.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀠󠀳 󠀰Judging by the notes in his notebook, he had almost realized that.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀡󠀳 󠀰But "almost" isn't enough for a man with a rifle.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀢󠀳There's a new file from the Sector 3 analysts on the table.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀣󠀳 󠀰This time, nobody's taking my target.

The wheels are in place.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀥󠀳 󠀰The Fossa is ready.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀦󠀳Internal Security found the source of the leak.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀧󠀳 󠀰A cryptographer.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀨󠀳 󠀰He worked with Erich during the war.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀩󠀳 󠀰Felt Sector 3 was moving too slowly.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀠󠀳 󠀰He was sending data on everyone who'd received information from the satellite.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀡󠀳 󠀰Even those we hadn't yet classified as targets.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀢󠀳 󠀰He was convinced there was no time to wait, but I still think the cost of a mistake is too high.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀣󠀳There's one detail that troubles me: some of the targets passed to Erich don't match any of Sector 3's lists.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀤󠀳 󠀰Either the cryptographer was conducting his own intelligence operations, or there was some third party giving him information from the outside.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀥󠀳 󠀰Perhaps he was using Erich the same way someone was using him.

󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀨󠀳󠀰󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀦󠀳The new file contains assignments on a different scale.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀧󠀳 󠀰Prototype weapons in the hands of people who know how to use them.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀨󠀳 󠀰For targets like these, a rifle's not enough—you need a different caliber. It's time to send the Fossa out to hunt.

We've installed the turret.󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀳 󠀰It's a solid construction, correctly aligned.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀳 󠀰Traverse speed is as I expected.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀨󠀳󠀰I'm back from Marseille.󠀲󠀡󠀩󠀳 󠀰Things didn't go as planned.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀢󠀠󠀳I took up the position four minutes ahead of the scheduled time.󠀲󠀢󠀡󠀳 󠀰A warehouse opposite the port, second floor.󠀲󠀢󠀢󠀳 󠀰Steady wind, comfortable distance.󠀲󠀢󠀣󠀳 󠀰Target's in my sights.󠀲󠀢󠀤󠀳 󠀰My finger's on the trigger.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀢󠀥󠀳Then a shot.󠀲󠀢󠀦󠀳 󠀰But not by me.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀢󠀧󠀳The target's eliminated.󠀲󠀢󠀨󠀳 󠀰Clean work.󠀲󠀢󠀩󠀳 󠀰Judging by the trajectory, the shot came from the right, a floor above me.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀣󠀠󠀳󠀰I checked the other position.󠀲󠀣󠀡󠀳 󠀰No casing, no prints.󠀲󠀣󠀢󠀳 󠀰The shooter covered their tracks.󠀲󠀣󠀣󠀳 󠀰Quick and clean.󠀲󠀣󠀤󠀳 󠀰This was no amateur or rival from a private outfit.󠀲󠀣󠀥󠀳 󠀰It was a professional of my level, or higher.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀣󠀦󠀳󠀲󠀣󠀧󠀳󠀰Someone else is working on my contract.󠀲󠀣󠀨󠀳 󠀰I don't like that.

The vehicle assembly's progressing as planned.󠀲󠀤󠀠󠀳 󠀰We've fitted the wheel hubs, brakes, and shafts.󠀲󠀤󠀡󠀳 󠀰They're good quality, and the tolerances are within spec.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀤󠀢󠀳󠀰I checked the other targets.󠀲󠀤󠀣󠀳 󠀰The second and third have already been taken out.󠀲󠀤󠀤󠀳 󠀰Same MO: single shot, clear position.󠀲󠀤󠀥󠀳 󠀰But this time there were traces.󠀲󠀤󠀦󠀳 󠀰The shooter was likely interrupted.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀤󠀧󠀳󠀰Who are they?󠀲󠀤󠀨󠀳 󠀰The shooter has my list: my targets, my priorities, my deadlines.󠀲󠀤󠀩󠀳 󠀰That's information only a select few people in Sector 3 have access to.󠀲󠀥󠀠󠀳 󠀰Either there's been a leak, or a parallel operation was authorized without my knowledge.󠀲󠀥󠀡󠀳 󠀰The latter is unlikely: Sector 3 doesn't deploy multiple operatives on the same assignment. The risk of them crossing paths is too high.󠀲󠀥󠀢󠀳 󠀰So it must have been a leak.󠀲󠀥󠀣󠀳 󠀰Somebody's passing information to an outside shooter.󠀲󠀥󠀤󠀳 󠀰I need to find the source.󠀲󠀥󠀥󠀳 󠀰The targets can wait.󠀲󠀥󠀦󠀳 󠀰Whoever's taking them out is more dangerous.

󠀰We've put in the hatches.󠀲󠀥󠀨󠀳 󠀰The crew ones are standard, but the ammo loading hatch is bigger to allow for quick, easy shell loading.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀥󠀩󠀳󠀲󠀦󠀠󠀳No problems so far with the assembly. But there are problems with the operation.󠀲󠀦󠀡󠀳 󠀲󠀦󠀢Who could have both access to our lists and these kinds of skills?󠀲󠀦󠀣󠀳 󠀰Sector 3 only has three active operatives:󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀦󠀤󠀳󠀰Scharf.󠀲󠀦󠀥󠀳 󠀰The most likely candidate.󠀲󠀦󠀦󠀳 󠀰An experienced sniper, but her MO is different: spotter, weather data, position prepared a day in advance.󠀲󠀦󠀧󠀳 󠀰This shooter operates differently.󠀲󠀦󠀨󠀳 󠀰No infrastructure, no team.󠀲󠀦󠀩󠀳 󠀰One rifle, one person.󠀲󠀧󠀠󠀳 󠀰No, this isn't her style.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀧󠀡󠀳󠀰Corvin.󠀲󠀧󠀢󠀳 󠀰He has access to all classified data, or almost all.󠀲󠀧󠀣󠀳 󠀰He's a strategist.󠀲󠀧󠀥󠀳 󠀰But small arms aren't his thing.󠀲󠀧󠀦󠀳 󠀰Last time he fired one was three years ago, on the firing range.󠀲󠀧󠀧󠀳 󠀰Doesn't fit.󠀲󠀧󠀨󠀳󠀲󠀢󠀳

Kotva. A close-quarters combat specialist with standard firearms training. From three hundred meters, he'd hit a target with a rifle. From six hundred, not likely. Not him.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀨󠀤󠀳Which means somebody's passing information out of Sector 3.

Oversaw installation of the gun mantlet.󠀲󠀨󠀦󠀳 󠀰I can't trust anyone else to assemble the weapon.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀨󠀧󠀳󠀰I'm back in Marseille.󠀲󠀨󠀨󠀳 󠀰Went to check the other shooter's position again, and found brass shavings in a gap between the concrete slabs.󠀲󠀨󠀩󠀳 Barely noticeable.󠀲󠀩󠀡󠀳 󠀰Somebody had reworked the casing by hand and filed down the bullet tip.󠀲󠀩󠀢󠀳 󠀰Tuned the aerodynamics to the specific distance and the local wind conditions.󠀲󠀩󠀣󠀳 󠀰Not a factory-made sniper round.󠀲󠀩󠀤󠀳 󠀰Hand-crafted, one-of-a-kind.󠀲󠀩󠀥󠀳 󠀰Whoever did this understands ballistics at a level far beyond the reach of most people.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀩󠀦󠀳I know the technique; I've been using it myself since the winter of '44.󠀲󠀩󠀧󠀳 󠀰But I didn't invent it.󠀲󠀩󠀩󠀳 󠀰I was taught it by a man who shouldn't be alive anymore.

We've installed the gun.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀡󠀳 󠀰And we managed to enhance its performance using documents obtained in the Marseille operation.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀢󠀳 󠀰Test firings delivered excellent results.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀣󠀳 󠀰The penetration power should be sufficient to destroy any secret prototypes that have fallen into the wrong hands.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀤󠀳I went to Tangier, where the second target was taken out.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀥󠀳 󠀰The shooter didn't manage to completely clear their position—there was a trace from their support.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀧󠀳A triangular bipod.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀨󠀳 󠀰Shifts the center of gravity to the left.󠀲󠀡󠀠󠀩󠀳 󠀰It's a non-standard design; these aren't mass-produced.󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀠󠀳 󠀰I've seen a support like this once before.󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀡󠀳 󠀰In '44, on the Swiss border.󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀢󠀳 󠀰The man who made it told me, "A factory-made bipod is a compromise.󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀣󠀳 󠀰And a compromise at over six hundred meters is a miss."󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀤󠀳󠀰That man died in '45. In a mountain river, with his pack on his back. The body was swept away.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀥󠀳Or so I thought, for seven years.󠀲󠀡󠀡󠀩󠀳 󠀰But now I think differently.

󠀰Vehicle assembly's coming along without any surprises.󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀡󠀳 󠀰We've connected the electronic aiming systems.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀢󠀳Nothing new in the investigation, unfortunately.󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀣󠀳 󠀰I was hoping to find evidence that would disprove my theories.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀤󠀳󠀰Naples, third elimination. The target was hit from above, at a steep angle.󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀧󠀳 󠀰The shooter was in a tree.󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀨󠀳 󠀰I found a branch, 15 centimeters in diameter. A plane tree.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀢󠀩󠀳󠀰To hold your balance on that kind of perch, compensate for recoil, and hit the target with the first shot—technically, it's borderline impossible.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀠󠀳 󠀰I only know four people capable of something like that.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀡󠀳 󠀰Three of them are definitely no longer in this world.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀢󠀳󠀰The fourth was presumed dead.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀣󠀳 󠀰In the winter of '44, he took out a sentry from a similar plane tree.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀤󠀳 󠀰When I asked him how it was even possible, he laughed and replied with a single word: Gleichgewicht. Balance.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀥󠀳Three pieces of evidence. The casing, the bipod, and the tree.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀦󠀳 󠀰You could dismiss each one individually.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀧󠀳 󠀰But not all of them together.󠀲󠀡󠀣󠀨󠀳 󠀰There's no doubt anymore: it's him.

We've loaded out the vehicle with everything we could need for field work, in any conditions.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀠󠀳 󠀰I'm used to that sort of thing.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀢󠀳󠀲󠀢󠀳

Ambushes, sabotage, crossing mountain passes in '43 and '44.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀣󠀳 󠀰And much of it with Erich Walther, my partner in SOE operations.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀤󠀳 󠀰The only man who shot as accurately as I did.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀥󠀳 󠀰Perhaps even better.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀦󠀳󠀰In '45, he crossed a line.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀧󠀳 󠀰He eliminated a target without authorization.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀨󠀳 󠀰An enemy officer with a very bad reputation.󠀲󠀡󠀤󠀩󠀳 󠀰Erich was sure the man deserved a bullet, so he took the decision himself.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀠󠀳 󠀰The organization doesn't forgive that sort of thing.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀡󠀳 󠀰To escape its control, he faked his own death.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀢󠀳󠀰For seven years, I believed he was dead.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀣󠀳 󠀰Now he's working on my targets, using my methods.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀤󠀳 󠀰But only for as long as there are names on my list.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀥󠀳 󠀰After that...I need to stop him before then.

We've fitted the smoke grenade launchers.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀨󠀳 󠀰They can lay down a smoke screen in three seconds.󠀲󠀡󠀥󠀩󠀳 󠀰Essential equipment for a vehicle that needs to make a quick exit from the operational zone and return to base.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀠󠀳󠀰If Erich is alive and working in Europe, he needs a base too.󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀡󠀳 󠀰I checked the old safe house in Switzerland—the one we used back in '44.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀢󠀳󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀣󠀳He was here.󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀤󠀳 󠀰Recently.󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀥󠀳 󠀰On the table, there's a map with targets marked on it. His notebook, filled with notes. A mask on the back of a chair. It's a crude, hand-made one, but the idea's the same: you put on a mask so that you stop being yourself during the operation.󠀲󠀡󠀦󠀦󠀳 󠀰So that someone else fires the shot.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀡󠀳 󠀰The person in the mask.󠀲󠀢󠀳

󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀢󠀳I read his list.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀣󠀳 󠀰Five targets match my Sector 3 assignment.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀤󠀳 󠀰Another four don't.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀥󠀳 󠀰They're names that don't appear in any of our records.󠀲󠀡󠀧󠀦󠀳 󠀰People Erich sentenced personally.
